To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2DSD theory accounts for the distributions and relationships between choice accuracy, decision time, confidence, and time pressure in a perceptual and a general knowledge task.

the 2 stage dynamic diffusion theory provides a parsimonious explanation of the interrelationships between choice, response time, and confidence in both a perceptuo-motor and general knowledge task, and that judges make their confidence judgments in a manner consistent to the optimal solution for the task.

a 2DSD model of choice, decision, and confidence accounts for all known relationships between the 3 performance measures and explains their distributions in both a perceptually based and a general knowledge task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain accumulates and integrates evidence to make a choice, how it makes a confidence judgment, and how these processes are related.
developing a unified theory of choice, response time, and confidence in a dynamic decision process.
the development of a theory of choice and decision time that can also be used to predict confidence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2 stage dynamic model of signal detection is the best model of human decision making available today.
the 2DSD model is the best theory available for explaining and predicting choice, decision time and confidence.
2DSD theory accounts for choice, decision time and confidence using a common underlying random walk process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2DSD model provides the most complete account of human decision making and confidence.
2DSD is a theory of choice and confidence and the interrelationships between the two.
the model provides the first unified account of choice, decision times, and confidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
choice, response or choice time, and confidence are all related in a systematic way.
the same underlying cognitive mechanism is used to produce all three performance measures.
the 3 most common measures of performance can all be explained by the 2DSD model.
